about: Graphics pass 2 (lane town2): species in the catalogue export (data/ark/behaviour-profiles.json, plus the signature-behaviours catalogue quotes) whose stored text puts them in rotting wood (under logs or bark, eating decaying wood) or whose caterpillars live on leaves. Made by rule (scratchpad deadwood-list.py): small invertebrate body plans, land zones; deadwood = the stored phrase names rotting/dead/fallen wood, logs or bark; leaves = a flying insect whose stored phrase puts its caterpillar on leaves, twigs, nettles or its food plant (not in soil or litter). Read by hand; ambiguous ones left out. The town gives them the logs and stumps of townDeadwood and the leafy patches beside them. No animal is added: only where the ones aboard live.

deadwood.name: Agrarian Sac Spider
deadwood.text: often overwintering in a thicker silk retreat under bark

deadwood.name: Amazonian Giant Centipede
deadwood.text: It shelters in leaf litter, under logs and stones, in rock crevices and in caves

deadwood.name: American Giant Millipede
deadwood.text: under logs or in soil

deadwood.name: Atlas Beetle
deadwood.text: decaying wood and organic matter

deadwood.name: Bold Jumper
deadwood.text: closed silk sac spun under bark

deadwood.name: Brazilian Wandering Spider
deadwood.text: It spends the day hidden in crevices, under logs and bark, in banana bunches or in dark corners of buildings, and comes out after dark to hunt.

deadwood.name: Bronze Ground Beetle
deadwood.text: It spends the day under logs, stones, bark or leaf litter and emerges after dusk

deadwood.name: Eciton Army Ant
deadwood.text: At night workers cluster into a hanging bivouac of linked bodies under logs or among roots

deadwood.name: Giant African Land Snail
deadwood.text: stones or logs

deadwood.name: Giant African Millipede
deadwood.text: Decaying leaves, rotting wood, soft fruit, and organic debris

deadwood.name: Giant Forest Scorpion
deadwood.text: They are nocturnal and often hide under logs, bark, or burrows by day

deadwood.name: Golden Stag Beetle
deadwood.text: By day they hide under bark, in leaf litter or among foliage

deadwood.name: Harvestman
deadwood.text: By day most hide under stones, logs, bark and leaves

deadwood.name: Hercules Beetle
deadwood.text: decaying wood

deadwood.name: Rainbow Stag Beetle
deadwood.text: in log cavities or in leaf litter

deadwood.name: Red Triangle Slug
deadwood.text: In dry weather it shelters under logs

deadwood.name: Semi-slug
deadwood.text: Through dry daylight hours it rests under leaves, logs, stones and in crevices where the air stays moist.

deadwood.name: Smooth Ground Beetle
deadwood.text: Mostly nocturnal, resting by day under logs, stones, moss or bark

deadwood.name: Termite
deadwood.text: Plant fiber, dead wood, grasses, and fungus gardens

deadwood.name: Trilobite Beetle
deadwood.text: Females appear to feed on liquids and soft material from rotting wood

deadwood.name: Walnut Orb-weaver
deadwood.text: Several individuals are sometimes found sheltering under the same piece of loose bark

deadwood.name: Woodlouse Hunter Spider
deadwood.text: log or loose bark

deadwood.name: Yellow-banded Millipede
deadwood.text: shelters by day under bark, stones, mulch and damp litter, emerging on humid nights

leaves.name: Cabbage Cluster Moth
leaves.text: The caterpillars shelter inside their webs and in the hearts of plants.

leaves.name: Common Marble
leaves.text: The caterpillar ties leaves or shoot tips together with silk and feeds hidden inside.

leaves.name: Emerald Moth
leaves.text: the caterpillar rests stretched stiffly along twigs, where it looks like a small shoot or bud

leaves.name: Geometer Moth
leaves.text: Many caterpillars stand rigid like a twig or drop on a silk line when disturbed

leaves.name: Giant Redeye
leaves.text: its caterpillar hides in a rolled palm leaf under a coat of fluffy white wax

leaves.name: Hackberry Emperor
leaves.text: Late-season caterpillars spend the winter in groups inside curled dead leaves and resume feeding in spring.

leaves.name: Mourning Cloak
leaves.text: lays eggs in a ring around a twig; caterpillars feed together under a shared silk web

leaves.name: Pale Beauty Moth
leaves.text: fringed looper caterpillar presses flat against a twig

leaves.name: Peacock Butterfly
leaves.text: caterpillars live together in a silk web on nettles

leaves.name: Red Admiral
leaves.text: The Red Admiral caterpillar pulls the edges of a nettle leaf together with silk and feeds alone inside the tent it has made.

leaves.name: Red-spotted Purple
leaves.text: The caterpillar rests in plain view on a leaf, its lumpy, mottled brown and white body resembling a fresh bird dropping.

leaves.name: Tiger Moth
leaves.text: Larvae rest beneath Ficus leaves and feed in groups after eggs are laid in batches.

leaves.name: Two-tailed Pasha
leaves.text: Caterpillars rest on a pad of silk spun on a leaf, returning to it between meals.

leaves.name: White Peacock Butterfly
leaves.text: Adults drink flower nectar, while caterpillars feed on host plant leaves

leaves.name: Zebra Swallowtail
leaves.text: Adults drink nectar from flowers, while caterpillars feed on pawpaw leaves
